title: Platform systems & services - dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and Q2 2025 retrospective
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This document consolidates the Platform Systems & Services operating artifacts: systems inventory, primary dashboards and alerting rules, runbooks for high-priority failure modes, a six-month roadmap, and the Q2 2025 retrospective with clear action items. It is intended as the primary reference for on-call engineers, platform owners, and cross-functional partners.

Scope
- Covers production-facing platform services owned by eng-platform: API gateway, routing service, inference runtime fleet, autoscaler, cache layer, and control-plane services (deployments, model catalog, telemetry).
- Includes dashboards (Grafana), alerting rules (Prometheus/Alertmanager), runbook procedures, and roadmap items relevant to platform reliability and operability.

Ownership
- Document owner: Platform Systems & Services (eng-platform).
- On-call: Platform SRE rotation (PagerDuty schedule: team-platsre-primary).
- Escalation: Platform Lead (Jordan Patel), Head of SRE (Samira Gupta).

Systems & Services Inventory (high level)
| Service | Primary responsibility | SLO | Key dashboard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| api-gateway | ingress, auth, routing | 99.95% availability | Platform / Gateway Overview |
| inference-runtime | model serving (hosted) | p99 latency < 250ms (short prompts) | Inference Fleet Health |
| autoscaler | scale pools for throughput | scale within 60s for burst | Autoscaler Activity |
| kv-cache | shared prefix/KV cache | cache hit rate > 75% | Cache Efficiency |
| control-plane | deployments, model catalog | 99.9% availability | Control Plane Health |

Dashboards & Alerts
Principles
- Dashboard names and panels should map to on-call responsibilities (owner annotation on dashboard).
- Alerts only page for actionable conditions; all alerts must link to a runbook.
- Alert severities: P0 (page), P1 (page + ticket), P2 (ticket), P3 (info).

Primary dashboards (examples)
- Platform Overview (team health summary): error rate, traffic, p50/p95/p99 latency, capacity utilization.
- Inference Fleet Health: per-pool CPU/GPU utilization, pod restarts, model-hotload failures, KV cache hit rate.
- Request Latency by Route: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings.
- Autoscaler Activity: scale events, queued requests, backpressure signals.

Example alerting rules (Prometheus style)
- High error rate (P0):
  ALERT PlatformHighErrorRate
  IF increase(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m]) > 0.03
  FOR 2m
  LABELS { severity="P0" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="api-gateway 5xx > 3% over 5m", runbook="/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/api-gateway-5xx" }

- Inference node OOM rate (P1):
  ALERT InferenceOOMRateHigh
  IF increase(kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled",namespace=~"production.*"}[15m]) > 3
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity="P1" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="High OOMKilled rate in inference namespace", runbook="/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/inference-oom" }

Runbooks (priority playbooks)
1) High CPU/GPU saturation on inference pool (P0/P1)
- Detection: alert InferencePoolHighUtilization fires or p99 latency spikes on Inference Fleet Health dashboard.
- Triage: identify affected pool (pool label), confirm whether CPU or GPU is saturated: use Prometheus queries: 
  - GPU util (nvidia): avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization{pool="<pool>"}[5m])
  - Pod CPU: sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"inference-.*"}[1m])) by (pod)
- Mitigation (ordered):
  1. If autoscaler is healthy, trigger manual scale: kubectl scale --replicas=<N+> deployment/<pool-deployment> -n production
  2. If autoscaler not responding, open CLI to control-plane: 
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/pools/<pool>/scale -d '{"target_replicas": <N>} ' 
  3. Evacuate heavy models: update rollout to move <model> to another pool (follow model-migration runbook).
  4. If degradation continues, enable degraded-mode routing: route non-critical traffic to lower-priority model-variants.
- Post-incident: capture latency histograms, add scoped alert thresholds if needed.

2) Full 5xx on /v1/generate (P0)
- Detection: PlatformHighErrorRate alert for api-gateway with runbook mapping.
- Triage: check upstream (inference-runtime) and control-plane errors:
  - kubectl logs -l app=api-gateway -n production --since=10m
  - curl -v https://inference-runtime.internal/healthz
- Mitigation:
  1. Identify if rollout caused regression: check recent deployment events (kubectl rollout history).
  2. If bad deployment found: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway -n production
  3. If dependency (model-serving) is failing, fail traffic to canary and route to fallback models using routing rules: POST /control-plane/route/fallback
  4. If outage persists > 15m, trigger cross-functional war room and notify product and solutions engineering.

On-call runbook checklist (quick)
1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create incident in Issue Tracker.
2. Add a short summary to the incident channel (#incident-platform).
3. Follow runbook steps and record actions as comments.
4. If paging escalation needed, follow escalation ladder in Ownership section.

How-tos (operational recipes)
- Adding a new Grafana dashboard
  1. Create dashboard JSON via local Grafonnet/provisioning templates.
  2. Validate panels using local dev Grafana instance (grafana-cli).
  3. Submit PR to infra/dashboards; include owner and alert mappings.
  4. After merge, trigger CI job infra-dashboards-provision to apply.

- Creating an alert rule
  1. Draft Prometheus rule under monitoring/alerts/platform/*.yaml with labels: severity, owner, runbook.
  2. Include a for: duration and a for_each_disabled: false (to avoid flapping).
  3. Add link to runbook in annotations.runbook.
  4. PR, review by two reviewers (monitoring and owning team).

Roadmap (next 6 months)
- Q3 2025: Consolidate and standardize all dashboard owners; map dashboards to SLOs (owner: Maya Chen).
- Q4 2025: Implement dynamic alert suppression during controlled rollouts and CI-driven alert testing (owner: Liam O'Neill).
- Q1 2026: Autoscaler rewrite for predictive scaling based on request forecasting (owner: Platform Team).
- Continued: Expand per-model observability (traces across control-plane -> runtime).

Q2 2025 Retrospective (summary)
- Incidents reviewed: 3 production-impacting events in Q2 (High inference latency spike on 2025-05-14, API gateway 5xx regression on 2025-06-03, Autoscaler thrash on 2025-06-28).
- Root causes: insufficient autoscaler backpressure handling, an unsafe rollout of model-hotload, and a misconfigured alert threshold that created alert fatigue.
- What went well: improved cross-team runbook coverage; successful rapid rollback on 2025-06-03 prevented longer outage.

Action items (owners & target dates)
- ACTION-PLAT-101: Reduce alert noise by raising non-actionable P3 thresholds and consolidating similar alerts (owner: Maya Chen, due: 2025-07-15).
- ACTION-PLAT-102: Add autoscaler health dashboard and preflight checks for rollouts (owner: Liam O'Neill, due: 2025-08-01).
- ACTION-PLAT-103: Formalize model-hotload canary procedure and automated rollback window (owner: Platform Team, due: 2025-09-01).
